question.text: Consider a rectangle <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi><mi>C</mi><mi>D</mi></math> having <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>9</mn></math> points in the interior of the line segments <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>B</mi><mi>C</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>C</mi><mi>D</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>D</mi><mi>A</mi></math> respectively. Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>α</mi></math> be the number of triangles having these points from different sides as vertices and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>β</mi></math> be the number of quadrilaterals having these points from different sides as vertices. Then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow></mfenced></math> is equal to

solution.text:
α= Number of triangles

α=5·6·7+5·7·9+5·6·9+6·7·9

=210+315+270+378

=1173

β= Number of Quadrilateral

β=5·6·7·9=1890

β-α=1890-1173=717
